data.narrative:
Caelux, a Series A climate and energy company founded by Scott Graybeal, is evaluated against a sector universe of 9 peers (1 public, 8 private) including Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, KoBold Metals, Electric Hydrogen, and Enovix. The target has raised $75M to date.

The valuation relies on a stage-progression methodology, which is applicable given Caelux's position within the frontier climate and energy investment landscape. This approach applies a 2.0x step-up multiplier to the $75M total raised, reflecting typical valuation expansion from Series A to subsequent rounds. This calculation yields an implied valuation of $150M. A peer-median approach was not viable; while 8 same-sector comparables exist, insufficient datapoints met narrow-stage and valuation-tier filters (zero same-stage and zero adjacent-stage matches), and relying on all-sector medians would introduce unwarranted noise. With only one applicable method, triangulation produces a range of $128M (low) to $172M (high), centered at $150M.

The analysis is constrained by limited comparable transaction data at Caelux's exact stage and subsector within climate tech. The $150M median should be treated as indicative rather than precise, pending visibility into recent Series A closings among direct peers or deeper operational metrics (revenue, cash burn, IP position). Key uncertainties include fundraising velocity in the sector and whether Caelux's technology and team command stage-typical multiples.
